learn.title: Educational mini-challenges
learn.subtitle: Learn key warning signs and earn points through short challenges.
learn.daily_rotation_desc: We show {{count}} challenges per day, rotating automatically from the scientific challenge bank.
learn.image_question_prompt: Which image corresponds to the malignant lesion?
learn.already_completed: This challenge is already completed. No extra points can be earned.
learn.daily_limit_reached: You already completed {{count}} challenges today. Come back tomorrow for more.
learn.points_awarded: Great job! You earned +{{points}} points and +{{xp}} XP.
learn.quiz_review_summary: Quiz submitted: {{correct}}/{{total}} correct answers. You earned +{{points}} points and +{{xp}} XP.
learn.select_answer: Please select an answer before submitting.
learn.review_correct: Correct answer. Points and XP awarded.
learn.review_wrong: Wrong answer. No points or XP were awarded for this question.
learn.start_desc: Start when you are ready. Answers are only evaluated at the end.
learn.challenge1_content: A: Asymmetry, B: Irregular borders, C: Multiple colors, D: Diameter above 6mm, E: Evolution over time.
learn.challenge2_content: Choose the best answer for identifying suspicious lesions.
learn.challenge2_question: Which sign should prompt medical evaluation?
learn.challenge2_opt1: A mole that quickly changed color and size over recent weeks.
learn.challenge2_opt2: A stable mole with no changes for years.
learn.challenge2_opt3: A spot that disappeared on its own after a few days.
learn.challenge2_source: AIM at Melanoma - diagnosis and warning signs
learn.challenge3_content: Look at the two photographs and choose the image corresponding to the malignant lesion.
learn.challenge3_image_content: Look at the two photographs and choose the image corresponding to the malignant lesion.
learn.challenge4_content: The higher the UV index, the lower the skin damage risk and the less protection is needed.
learn.challenge5_content: Test your knowledge about safer sun exposure.
learn.challenge5_question: During which period is UV risk usually highest?
learn.challenge6_content: A monthly skin self-exam is not useful for detecting early changes in lesions.
learn.challenge6_source: AAD - how to perform a skin self-exam
learn.challenge7_content: Understanding SPF helps you use sunscreen correctly.
learn.challenge7_question: Which statement about SPF is correct?
learn.challenge7_opt1: SPF 30 blocks a large share of UVB radiation when properly applied.
learn.challenge7_opt2: High SPF completely removes the need to reapply.
learn.challenge8_content: Wide-brim hats, UV-protective sunglasses, and appropriate clothing reduce cumulative UV exposure and complement sunscreen.
learn.challenge9_title: Quiz: Sign that needs quick assessment
learn.challenge9_content: Not every spot is dangerous, but some signs need rapid evaluation.
learn.challenge9_question: Which situation should prompt priority medical assessment?
learn.challenge9_opt1: A lesion that bleeds easily and is changing its appearance.
learn.challenge9_opt2: A mole unchanged for many years.
learn.challenge9_source: CDC - skin cancer signs and symptoms
learn.challenge10_content: A sore that persists for weeks without healing can be a warning sign and should be checked by dermatology.
learn.challenge10_source: AAD - signs of common skin cancers
learn.challenge11_content: Sunscreen effectiveness depends on proper reapplication.
learn.challenge11_question: What is the most appropriate recommendation outdoors?
learn.challenge11_opt1: Reapply every 2 hours and after swimming or heavy sweating.
learn.challenge11_opt2: Applying only in the morning is enough for the whole day.
learn.challenge12_content: Consistent photo records do not help detect lesion evolution over time during follow-up.
learn.challenge12_source: Clinical evidence in dermoscopy and photographic monitoring
learn.challenge13_content: Fair skin, family history, many nevi, and repeated sunburns increase melanoma risk.
learn.challenge14_content: Artificial UV exposure also has a relevant effect on skin health.
learn.challenge14_question: Which statement about tanning beds is correct?
learn.challenge14_opt1: Tanning beds increase skin cancer risk and premature aging.
learn.challenge14_opt2: Tanning beds are a safe way to prepare skin for summer.
learn.challenge14_opt3: Tanning bed radiation does not affect skin DNA.
learn.challenge15_content: Applying too little sunscreen reduces protection. A practical adult full-body amount is about 30 ml.
learn.challenge16_content: Not all sunscreens provide the same UV coverage.
learn.challenge16_question: What does 'broad spectrum' on sunscreen mean?
learn.challenge16_opt1: It protects against both UVA and UVB.
learn.challenge16_opt3: It only moisturizes without UV protection.
learn.challenge17_content: Sun protection in childhood is critical because early sunburns are associated with higher future risk.
learn.challenge18_content: Asymmetry can be a warning sign in the ABCDE context.
learn.challenge18_opt1: One half of the lesion looks different from the other.
learn.challenge18_opt2: A round symmetrical lesion with no changes.
learn.challenge18_source: American Cancer Society - melanoma warning signs
learn.challenge19_content: Higher-risk people do not benefit from regular dermatology follow-up for early detection.
learn.challenge19_source: British Association of Dermatologists - skin cancer
learn.challenge20_title: Quiz: When to seek medical care
learn.challenge20_content: Timely action can make a difference in early detection.
learn.challenge20_question: When should you seek medical assessment for a lesion?
learn.challenge20_opt1: When it changes, bleeds, forms persistent crust, or does not heal.
learn.challenge20_opt2: Only if there is intense pain.
learn.challenge21_content: Compare the two dermoscopy images and select the malignant lesion confirmed in ISIC metadata.
learn.challenge21_source: ISIC Archive - invasive melanoma and benign nevus
learn.challenge22_content: Look at both images and choose the malignant lesion. One is classified in ISIC as melanoma in situ.
learn.challenge22_source: ISIC Archive - melanoma in situ and benign nevus
learn.challenge23_content: Compare the two images and choose the malignant lesion confirmed by histopathology in ISIC Archive.
learn.challenge23_source: ISIC Archive - melanoma in situ and benign nevus
learn.challenge24_content: Some personal and family history factors increase skin cancer risk.
learn.challenge24_question: Which factor can increase skin cancer risk?
learn.challenge24_opt1: Family history of skin cancer or a history of sunburns.
learn.challenge25_content: On cloudy days and in winter, skin is no longer exposed to UV radiation.
learn.challenge25_source: AAD - sun protection on cloudy days
learn.challenge26_question: When should you apply sunscreen before going outdoors?
learn.challenge26_opt2: Only after the skin starts turning red.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: To help you take care of your skin, we need to process some data. Here is how we do it simply:
privacy.security_highlight: Your data is not shared with third parties without your consent.

topics.identity_desc: We store your name, birth year, and health history to personalize scan frequency recommendations. Our system suggests when to examine your skin based on your risk profile.
topics.photos_desc: The photos you take of your lesions never leave your phone. Processing is done locally to ensure that no one but you has access to these images.
topics.admin_desc: Platform administrators only manage statistical data and the challenge system. They do not have access to your private medical images or diagnoses.
topics.admin_desc2: Your data is not shared with third parties without your consent.
topics.purpose_desc: The sole purpose of processing this data is the prevention and monitoring of your skin health, encouraging healthy habits through challenges and reminders.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: By using Nevo, you agree to the following conditions of use to ensure your safety and the platform's effectiveness:

topics.medical_desc: Nevo is an awareness tool. AI results are indicative and do not, under any circumstances, replace direct observation by a doctor.
topics.usage_desc: The user commits to providing truthful data and using image capture as instructed to ensure the best possible analysis.
topics.liability_desc: The platform is not responsible for self-diagnosis. If you notice any change in a lesion, you must seek immediate medical assistance.
